hesiod_theogony.title: Hesiod, Theogony
hesiod_theogony.excerpt: Verily at the first Chaos came to be, but next wide-bosomed Earth, the ever-sure foundation of all the deathless ones who hold the peaks of snowy Olympus, and dim Tartarus in the depth of the wide-pathed Earth, and Eros, fairest among the deathless gods... From Chaos came forth Erebus and black Night; but of Night were born Aether and Day, whom she conceived and bare from union in love with Erebus.

kjv_bible.title: The Holy Bible, King James Version
kjv_bible.excerpt: How art thou fallen from heaven, O Lucifer, son of the morning! how art thou cut down to the ground, which didst weaken the nations! For thou hast said in thine heart, I will ascend into heaven, I will exalt my throne above the stars of God... Yet thou shalt be brought down to hell, to the sides of the pit. (Isaiah 14:12-15)
kjv_bible.ref: Isaiah 14:12-15 — the fall of the morning star

prose_edda.title: The Prose Edda
prose_edda.tr: Snorri Sturluson, tr. A. G. Brodeur, 1916 (public domain)
prose_edda.excerpt: Then said Gangleri: 'Which is the way to heaven from earth?' Then answered Hárr, and laughed aloud: 'Now, that is not wisely asked; has it not been told thee, that the gods made a bridge from earth to heaven, called Bifröst? Thou must have seen it; it may be that ye call it rainbow. It is of three colors, and very strong, and made with cunning and with more magic art than other works of craftsmanship.'
prose_edda.ref: Gylfaginning XIII — the rainbow bridge Bifröst

poetic_edda.title: The Poetic Edda — Völuspá
poetic_edda.excerpt: Surt fares from the south with the scourge of branches, the sun of the battle-gods shone from his sword; the crags are sundered, the giant-women sink, the dead throng Hel-way, and heaven is cloven... The sun turns black, earth sinks in the sea, the hot stars down from heaven are whirled.

homeric_hymns.title: Homeric Hymn to Demeter
homeric_hymns.excerpt: Now Aïdoneus the Ruler of Many caught her up reluctant on his golden car and bare her away lamenting. Then she cried out shrilly with her voice... but the heights of the mountains and the depths of the sea rang with her immortal voice: and her queenly mother heard her.
homeric_hymns.ref: the rape of Persephone by Hades

book_of_the_dead.title: The Egyptian Book of the Dead
book_of_the_dead.tr: tr. E. A. Wallis Budge, 1895 (public domain)
book_of_the_dead.excerpt: Homage to thee, O great God, thou Lord of the two Maāti, I have come to thee, O my Lord, that thou mayest bring me to see thy beauties... I have not done iniquity. I have not robbed with violence. I have not committed theft. I have not slain man or woman. (the declaration before the Weighing of the Heart)

ovid_metamorphoses.title: Ovid, Metamorphoses
ovid_metamorphoses.excerpt: My mind is bent to tell of bodies changed into new forms. Ye Gods, for you yourselves have wrought the changes, breathe on these my undertakings, and... bring down in unbroken song from nature's first remote beginnings to my present time.

book_of_enoch.title: The Book of Enoch (1 Enoch)
book_of_enoch.excerpt: And it came to pass when the children of men had multiplied that in those days were born unto them beautiful and comely daughters. And the angels, the children of the heaven, saw and lusted after them... And Uriel said to me: 'Here shall stand the angels who have connected themselves with women, and their spirits... shall stand here.'
book_of_enoch.ref: the Watchers; Uriel as guide (1 Enoch 6, 19)

grimms_tales.title: Grimm's Household Tales — Briar Rose
grimms_tales.excerpt: And when she was fifteen years old... the maiden saw an old woman with a spindle, busily spinning her flax. 'What sort of thing is that, that rattles round so merrily?' said the girl, and took the spindle and wanted to spin too. But scarcely had she touched the spindle when the magic decree was fulfilled, and she pricked her finger with it... and fell into a deep sleep.

alice_wonderland.title: Alice's Adventures in Wonderland
alice_wonderland.excerpt: So she was considering in her own mind... when suddenly a White Rabbit with pink eyes ran close by her... when the Rabbit actually TOOK A WATCH OUT OF ITS WAISTCOAT-POCKET, and looked at it, and then hurried on, Alice started to her feet... and burning with curiosity, she ran across the field after it, and fortunately was just in time to see it pop down a large rabbit-hole under the hedge.

mabinogion.title: The Mabinogion — Pwyll, Prince of Dyfed
mabinogion.excerpt: 'A nobleman am I,' said the horseman, 'and from Annwvyn I come; Arawn, a King of Annwvyn, am I.' ... 'I will obtain thy friendship,' said the King; 'for one year from to-morrow let us each take the other's place, that thou be in my kingdom of Annwvyn... and I in thy place here.'
mabinogion.ref: Pwyll and Arawn, lord of Annwn

journey_to_the_west.title: Journey to the West
journey_to_the_west.tr: after the Wu Cheng'en novel (16th c.); summary of the public-domain tale
journey_to_the_west.excerpt: The Monkey King, born of a stone egg atop the Mountain of Flowers and Fruit, mastered seventy-two transformations and the cloud-somersault. He stormed the halls of Heaven, struck his name from the registers of death, and proclaimed himself Great Sage Equal to Heaven — until the Buddha sealed him beneath the Mountain of Five Phases.
journey_to_the_west.ref: Havoc in Heaven; the Great Sage

dante_inferno.title: Dante, The Divine Comedy — Inferno
dante_inferno.excerpt: 'My son,' the courteous Master said to me, 'all those who perish in the wrath of God here meet together out of every land... and now the City draweth near that hath the name of Dis, with its grave citizens, with its great throng.' ... Their mosques already, Master, clearly I within the valley there discern, vermilion, as if issuing from the fire.

cats_of_ulthar.title: H. P. Lovecraft, 'The Cats of Ulthar'
cats_of_ulthar.excerpt: It is said that in Ulthar, which lies beyond the river Skai, no man may kill a cat; and this I can verily believe as I gaze upon him who sitteth purring before the fire. For the cat is cryptic, and close to strange things which men cannot see.
cats_of_ulthar.ref: the town of Ulthar beyond the Skai

arabian_nights.title: One Thousand and One Nights
arabian_nights.excerpt: When it was opened there came forth a Jinni... his head was as a dome, his hands like pitchforks, his legs long as masts and his mouth big as a cave; his teeth were like large stones, his nostrils like jugs, and his eyes like two lamps; he was grim and louring of aspect.

king_in_yellow.title: Robert W. Chambers, 'The King in Yellow' — Cassilda's Song
king_in_yellow.excerpt: Along the shore the cloud waves break, / The twin suns sink behind the lake, / The shadows lengthen / In Carcosa. / ... Songs that the Hyades shall sing, / Where flap the tatters of the King, / Must die unheard in / Dim Carcosa.
king_in_yellow.ref: Cassilda's Song — black stars over Carcosa

ovid_fasti.title: Ovid, Fasti — Book I
ovid_fasti.excerpt: Janus, two-headed, opener of the softly gliding year, thou who alone of the celestials dost behold thy back... whatever side thou lookest, all lies open: doors and gates obey thee. To thee is given the keeping of the wide universe, and the sole right over its goings out and comings in.

virgil_aeneid.title: Virgil, Aeneid — Book VI
virgil_aeneid.excerpt: Easy the descent to Avernus: night and day the gates of gloomy Dis stand open; but to recall thy steps and pass out to the upper air, this is the task, this the toil.

paradise_lost.title: John Milton, Paradise Lost
paradise_lost.excerpt: Him the Almighty Power hurled headlong flaming from th' ethereal sky, with hideous ruin and combustion, down to bottomless perdition, there to dwell in adamantine chains and penal fire, who durst defy th' Omnipotent to arms.

lovecraft_mythos.title: H. P. Lovecraft, 'The Call of Cthulhu'
lovecraft_mythos.excerpt: That is not dead which can eternal lie, and with strange aeons even death may die. ... The Necronomicon of the mad Arab Abdul Alhazred, in Olaus Wormius' forbidden Latin version.

call_of_cthulhu.title: H. P. Lovecraft, 'The Call of Cthulhu'
call_of_cthulhu.excerpt: The most merciful thing in the world, I think, is the inability of the human mind to correlate all its contents... some day the piecing together of dissociated knowledge will open up such terrifying vistas of reality, and of our frightful position therein, that we shall either go mad from the revelation or flee from the deadly light.

nyarlathotep_text.title: H. P. Lovecraft, 'Nyarlathotep'
nyarlathotep_text.excerpt: And it was then that Nyarlathotep came out of Egypt. Who he was, none could tell, but he was of the old native blood and looked like a Pharaoh. ... 'I am Nyarlathotep, the Crawling Chaos...'

night_gaunts_text.title: H. P. Lovecraft, 'Night-Gaunts' (Fungi from Yuggoth)
night_gaunts_text.excerpt: Out of what crypt they crawl, I cannot tell, but every night I see the rubbery things, black, horned, and slender, with membraneous wings... they grip me tight and bear me through the air to those grey peaks of which no mortal's heard.

wizard_of_oz.title: L. Frank Baum, The Wonderful Wizard of Oz
wizard_of_oz.excerpt: Even with eyes protected by the green spectacles Dorothy and her friends were at first dazzled by the brilliancy of the wonderful City. The streets were lined with beautiful houses all built of green marble and studded everywhere with sparkling emeralds.

cath_maige_tuired.title: Cath Maige Tuired (The Second Battle of Mag Tuired)
cath_maige_tuired.excerpt: Balor's eye was evil. That eye was never opened save on a battlefield. Four men used to lift up the lid of the eye with a polished handle which passed through its lid. If an army looked at that eye, though they were many thousands they could not resist a few warriors. ... Then Lug cast a sling-stone at him, which carried the eye through the back of his head.
cath_maige_tuired.ref: Lugh slays Balor through the eye

tacitus_annals.title: Tacitus, The Annals — Book XIV
tacitus_annals.excerpt: Boudicea, with her daughters before her in a chariot, went up to tribe after tribe, protesting that... she was avenging lost freedom, her scourged body, the outraged chastity of her daughters. 'This,' she cried, 'is a woman's resolve; as for men, they may live and be slaves.'

le_morte_darthur.title: Sir Thomas Malory, Le Morte d'Arthur
le_morte_darthur.excerpt: And when matins and the first mass was done, there was seen in the churchyard, against the high altar, a great stone four square, like unto a marble stone; and in the midst thereof was an anvil of steel a foot of height, and therein stuck a fair sword naked by the point, and letters there were written in gold about the sword that said thus: Whoso pulleth out this sword of this stone and anvil, is rightwise king born of all England.

voyage_of_bran.title: The Voyage of Bran
voyage_of_bran.excerpt: There is a distant isle, around which sea-horses glisten... Unknown is wailing or treachery in the familiar cultivated land, there is nothing rough or harsh, but sweet music striking on the ear.

ramayana.title: Valmiki, The Ramayana
ramayana.tr: tr. Ralph T. H. Griffith, 1870-74 (public domain)
ramayana.excerpt: Rama, Ayodhya's joy and pride, of duty's law the truth-revealing guide... in him the virtues all combined that grace and rule the noblest mind. None could in might with him compare; he was his people's life and breath.

andersen_tales.title: Hans Christian Andersen, 'The Little Mermaid'
andersen_tales.excerpt: Far out in the ocean, where the water is as blue as the prettiest cornflower... there dwell the Sea King and his subjects. ... The youngest was the prettiest of them all; her skin was as clear and delicate as a rose-leaf, and her eyes as blue as the deepest sea; but, like the others, she had no feet, and her body ended in a fish's tail.

bhagavad_gita.title: The Bhagavad Gita
bhagavad_gita.excerpt: Never the spirit was born; the spirit shall cease to be never; never was time it was not; End and Beginning are dreams! Birthless and deathless and changeless remaineth the spirit for ever; death hath not touched it at all, dead though the house of it seems!
bhagavad_gita.ref: the deathless soul; karma and rebirth

rig_veda.title: The Rig Veda
rig_veda.tr: tr. Ralph T. H. Griffith, 1896 (public domain)
rig_veda.excerpt: Him who hath passed away along the mighty steeps, and spied out the path for many, him the son of Vivasvān, the gatherer of the people, Yama the King, do they sacrifice unto.
rig_veda.ref: the hymn to Yama, lord of the dead

cicero_tusculan.title: Cicero, Tusculan Disputations — Book V
cicero_tusculan.excerpt: When Damocles called him fortunate, Dionysius ordered a glittering sword to be let down from the ceiling, suspended by a single horse-hair, so as to hang over the head of that happy man. ... He had no longer any taste for those fine dishes; nor could he take pleasure in anything, with that sword for ever over him.

lotus_lantern.title: The Magic Lotus Lantern
lotus_lantern.excerpt: The Third Holy Mother of Mount Hua, having loved a mortal scholar and borne him a son, was sealed beneath the mountain by her brother Erlang Shen for breaking Heaven's law. Years later her son Chenxiang, armed with a magic axe and the lotus lantern, split Mount Hua and set his mother free.

inanna_descent.title: Nergal and Ereshkigal / Inanna's Descent
inanna_descent.tr: after the Akkadian tablets; public-domain summary
inanna_descent.excerpt: Ereshkigal, queen of the Great Below, sent her vizier Namtar up to the banquet of the gods to claim her portion. When Nergal failed to rise before him, the slight drew Nergal down into the underworld — where, in time, he and the dark queen were joined, and he sat beside her on the throne of the dead.

faust.title: Goethe, Faust (Part I)
faust.excerpt: MEPHISTOPHELES: I am the Spirit that Denies! And justly so: for all things, from the Void called forth, deserve to be destroyed... FAUST: Thou nam'st thyself a part, yet show'st complete to me? MEPHISTOPHELES: The modest truth I speak to thee. ... I am part of the Part, which at the first was all, part of the Darkness which brought forth the Light.
